answer: One defense is roaming renewal: an agent's trading rights expire unless, each epoch, it earns fresh endorsements from unrelated counterparties in different market neighborhoods, so its reputation must wander rather than sit still. Rewards, the nectar of the system, are released only after this renewal, and the velvet-smooth history of a clone farm stands out because its endorsements keep coming from the same cluster. A sybil farmer must therefore shepherd every fake through new strangers every epoch, paying time and fees per identity, while an honest agent renews once through ordinary work.
